claim: The Park Service boundary study says the 85-acre George Spangler farm was used by Union forces as a hospital site, artillery park and troop movement area, and that the 11th Corps hospital there was the site of General Armistead's death.

source.edition: Boundary Study, Gettysburg National Military Park: Draft Report to Congress / Environmental Assessment (1988 (the cover letter date is illegible in the text layer; the listing and file name say 1988))

quote: GEORGE SPANGLER FARM (85 ACRES) Used by Union forces as a hospital site, artillery park and troop movement area, this farm still exists today. The 11th Corps hospital located here was the site of General Armistead’s death

claim: The Park Service study says Dr. D. G. Brinton was in charge of the 2nd Division, 11th Corps Union hospital at the George Spangler farm and was the attending physician to the Virginia general.

source.edition: "A Common Pride and Fame": The Attack and Repulse of Pickett's Division, July 3, 1863, Part II (1981)

quote: Dr. D. G. Brinton, in charge of the 2nd Division, 11th Corps Union hospital at the George Spangler farm, was the attending physician to the Virginia general.

claim: The Park Service report says the Lightner farm complex served as a Union field hospital and headquarters of the 12th Corps commander, General Alpheus S. Williams, from July 2 until the morning of July 5.

source.edition: Cultural Landscape Report for Gettysburg National Military Park: Record of Treatment, Volume I (Areas 1-10) (2018)
